card.title: Rate law and Arrhenius — order, then energy barrier

rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Thermodynamics says IF; kinetics says how FAST. Rate = −d[reactant]/dt, set by concentration (rate law, exponents = ORDER, found experimentally — never read off the equation), temperature (Arrhenius: k = Ae^(−Ea/RT)), surface area, and catalysts (new lower-Ea path, same ΔH). Integrated forms linearise the data: zero order [A] vs t, first order ln[A] vs t (half-life constant).

rows.label: Formula
rows.text: rate = k[A]^m[B]^n (order m+n, experimental!)  ·  zero: [A] = [A]₀ − kt  ·  first: ln[A] = ln[A]₀ − kt, t½ = 0.693/k  ·  Arrhenius: k = A·e^(−Ea/RT) · log(k₂/k₁) = (Ea/2.303R)(1/T₁ − 1/T₂)

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: Rate laws describe elementary-rate behaviour at fixed T — change T, change k. Order ≠ molecularity ≠ stoichiometric coefficients (the classic trap). First-order half-life is concentration-independent ONLY for true first order. Arrhenius needs a single dominant barrier.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: N₂O₅ decomposition, radioactive decay, most hydrolyses: first order (t½ constant). Zero order: surface-saturated catalysis, photochemical (rate = constant while lit). Catalysts appear in neither rate law nor K — they only lower Ea. Rough rule: ~2× rate per 10 K rise.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: First-order test: plot ln[A] vs t — straight line slope −k confirms order and yields k; t½ = 0.693/k follows without further data. Arrhenius use: two k values at two T give Ea from the log ratio — activation energy from thermostats, not theory.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: Rate laws are empirical snapshots — mechanisms hide behind them (slow step rules). Arrhenius bends for tunnelling, diffusion control and complex multi-barrier paths. Order can be fractional or negative; 'order = coefficients' is wrong until proven by experiment.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: First order: d[A]/dt = −k[A] → separate → ∫d[A]/[A] = −k∫dt → ln[A] = ln[A]₀ − kt; half: ln(1/2) = −kt½ → t½ = 0.693/k. Zero order: d[A]/dt = −k → straight line. Arrhenius: fraction of molecules above Ea is e^(−Ea/RT) (Maxwell–Boltzmann tail) → k inherits the exponential.

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Order questions: method of initial rates (vary one concentration, watch ratio) or integrated-plot linearity. t½ constant → first order, instantly. Arrhenius: log form, two-point version. Catalyst: lowers Ea, unchanged K and ΔH — chant it.

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: NEB-style: order vs molecularity with examples; first-order integrated law + t½ derivation; Arrhenius statement with Ea-from-two-temperatures numerical; catalyst effect on Ea/K/ΔH.
